narrative.title: Longest Balanced Window in a Credit Ledger
narrative.scenario: A settlement ledger records signed credits per interval, and a balanced window is a contiguous run whose credits cancel out to zero. The auditors want the widest such window to sample, since it hides the largest stretch of offsetting activity. Credits may be positive or negative, so cumulative totals can wander.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n and an array A of n signed integers.
narrative.outputFormat: The length of the longest contiguous subarray whose elements sum to zero, or 0 when no such subarray exists.

testCases.explanation: The window -2,2,-8,1,7 cancels completely and spans five intervals, the widest such run.
The opening pair cancels to zero and gives a balanced window of length 2.

hintLevels: Level 1: A window sums to zero exactly when the running totals just before and just after it are equal.
Level 2: Remember the earliest index at which each running total appears and, on seeing a repeat, measure the distance from that first occurrence.
Level 3: Keep only the first occurrence of each total - overwriting it shrinks the window - and seed the empty prefix at index -1 so windows that begin at the first element are counted.
